about.body: The M256 is Mercedes-Benz's modern 3.0-litre inline-six petrol engine, introduced in 2017. It's a key part of the brand's move to a modular, electrified engine family, featuring an integrated starter-generator (ISG), an electric auxiliary compressor (e-boost), and a 48V mild-hybrid system as standard. It's fitted across five model lines, including the AMG GT 53, C 43 AMG, E 53 AMG, GLE 450, GLE 53 AMG, GLS 450, and GLS 580.

byModel.body: The M256 appears in the AMG GT as the GT 53, in the C-Class as the C 43 AMG, and in the E-Class as the E 53 AMG. Across the SUV range, it's the six-cylinder petrol option in the GLE-Class (as both the GLE 450 and GLE 53 AMG) and the GLS (as the GLS 450 and GLS 580). These applications are split across standard and AMG-tuned variants.

compatibility.body: All M256 applications are 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrids. However, standard and AMG variants differ in power output and specific tuning. The specific 48V MHEV system components, including the ISG and e-boost, also vary by application and generation. We confirm compatibility by registration/VIN before quoting any work.
